items.q: When did adolescent mental health curves "hockey-stick"?
items.a: Especially for **girls around ~2012** — anxiety, depression, self-harm, ER visits, and hospital admissions all inflect. Boys rise earlier (~**2009**) and more gradually. International data replicate it — not just Gen Z "talking more."

items.q: What is the great rewiring of childhood?
items.a: Between **2010–2015**, **play-based childhood** was replaced by **phone-based childhood** — outdoor free play traded for always-on, for-profit platforms during the **puberty sensitive period** for identity and social learning.

sections.title: Why puberty + feeds is the worst combo

items.q: Why is middle-school phone access uniquely dangerous?
items.a: Puberty opens **plasticity for identity, relationships, and social learning** exactly when parental control drops — and we hand kids **pocket internet + algorithmic extremity**. Prestige = likes → kids become **brand managers**, not players.

items.q: How do girls' and boys' harm patterns differ?
items.a: Girls show a sharp **2012 anxiety/depression/self-harm spike** tied heavily to social comparison apps; boys' smoother rise is driven more by **video, porn, and gaming**.

sections.title: Four norms that break the trap

items.q: What are Haidt's four phone norms?
items.a: **Delay devices and social media past plasticity**, remove phones from school, and restore real-world adventure — plus coordinated community norms. **"Keep in pocket"** fails; use Yondr pouches/lockers. TikTok in class teaches the wrong dopamine loops.

items.q: Why can't one family solve this alone?
items.a: It's a **collective action trap**: every 10-year-old "needs" a phone because peers have one. Solo delay **imposes a cost** on your child; simultaneous shifts (Let Grow, phone-free schools) break the lonely-kid problem.

items.q: Why aren't Fortnite and Instagram enough "adventure"?
items.a: **"Virtual adventures are just not going to cut it."** Kids need real independence — fort-building, boredom that reveals preferences, and **dynamic subordination groups** (sports, drill, dance) that teach hierarchy without toxicity.

items.q: What adult and policy tools does the episode recommend?
items.a: Phone-free meals, family group chats over DMs, **awe walks**, summer camp/team sports/religion as buffers, and advocacy for **KOSA**. Platforms extract attention like **casinos** under Section 230 — trauma images occupy **neural real estate** permanently.
